name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>. Descriptor accurately captures the behavior verified in body+disasm+callers: walk a straight 4-cardinal line collecting char indices that pass a team filter. No address residue in the name; no domain-ID suffixes involved.
purpose: Walk a straight 4-cardinal line from a start tile toward a target tile and collect the indices of characters on each in-bounds step whose team matches a filter; used for line/piercing targeting (line spell 0x1E and long-range projectile items).
logic_summary: Saves the global battle cursor (cursor_world_x/y). Picks a 4-cardinal step direction: pure vertical (dy=+1 if start_y<=target_y else -1) when start_x==target_x, otherwise pure horizontal toward target_x (dx=-1 left / +1 right); no diagonal stepping. Sets the cursor to (start_x,start_y), then loops step=0..step_count-1: advance cursor by (dx,dy); if the cursor is within [0,map_width_tiles) x [0,map_height_tiles), call fd2_find_char_at_cursor_pos(); if a char is present (idx != -1) and its team byte (offset +6, stride RUNTIME_CHAR_SIZE=0x50) satisfies the filter (filter==0 -> team!=0; filter!=0 -> team==0), append the char index (as a byte) to out_buf and increment hit_count. Restores the saved cursor and returns hit_count. Disassembly at 0x14ac2/0x14ad0-0x14ade confirms the index*5*16 (=*0x50) stride into runtime_char_array_ptr and the +6 team byte.
signature: int __cdecl fd2_scan_chars_along_line_with_team_filter(uint32 target_x, uint32 target_y, uint32 out_buf, uint32 start_x, uint32 start_y, uint32 step_count, uint32 team_filter)

params.name: target_x
params.semantics: X tile the line is aimed at (used only to decide step direction). Callers pass cursor_world_x or ai_best_item_target_x.
params.reason: Accurate, no address residue, matches all three call sites.

params.name: target_y
params.semantics: Y tile the line is aimed at (used to decide vertical direction). Callers pass cursor_world_y or ai_best_item_target_y.
params.reason: Accurate, no address residue, matches all three call sites.

params.name: out_buf
params.semantics: Output byte buffer; collected char indices are written sequentially (out_buf[hit_count] = (uint8)char_idx).
params.reason: Accurate; callers pass target_buf / target_idxs / target_id_buffer.

params.name: start_x
params.semantics: X origin of the line = caster position (caster.bPos_x in AI callers; saved pre-input cursor x in the spell-menu caller).
params.reason: Accurate, no address residue, matches all call sites.

params.name: start_y
params.semantics: Y origin of the line = caster position (caster.bPos_y in AI callers; saved pre-input cursor y in the spell-menu caller).
params.reason: Accurate, no address residue, matches all call sites.

params.name: step_count
params.semantics: Number of tiles to walk = range_class - 0x10 (the projectile/line range) at all three call sites.
params.reason: Accurate; loop bound is step_count; no address residue.

params.name: team_filter
params.semantics: Team selector: 0 collects chars on a non-zero team (enemy of player team 0); non-zero collects team-0 chars. Read into EDI; both AI callers pass 0, the spell-0x1E caster passes 1.
params.reason: Accurate and descriptive of the filter polarity; no address residue.

returns.semantics: hit_count -- number of matching char indices written into out_buf.

comment_original_issue: Original src comment was correct but terse: it omitted the team_filter polarity, the temporary clobber/restore of the global battle cursor, and the line-spell/projectile-item call context.
notes: Verified against decompile + disassembly (idx*0x50 stride, +6 team byte) and all three callers (fd2_spell_selection_menu_main spell 0x1E with team_filter=1; fd2_execute_ai_item_use and fd2_ai_score_item_use long-range item branch with team_filter=0, start = caster bPos_x/bPos_y). globals.h symbol names cross-checked against decompile (data_fd2_battle_*). cursor_world_y assigned before cursor_world_x in C source vs disasm order is a cosmetic reorder only (independent stores); not a logic concern.
